prompt.context: Our client, DigiBooks, is a manufacturer and seller of electronic book readers (tablets). DigiBooks also distributes e-books for the tablets through their website. The tablet is only compatible with books sold through the DigiBooks site. DigiBooks is planning the launch of its tablets in a country where no electronic book readers are currently sold. Only 1% of the population has ever used an electronic book reader, though 50% is aware of the concept.
prompt.question: The Chief Marketing Officer of DigiBooks has come to you to help determine: How should DigiBooks launch and market DigiBook tablets in this new country?

clarifying_info.q: What is an electronic book reader?
clarifying_info.a: A software, hardware and network platform that utilizes wireless connectivity to enable users to shop for, download, browse, and read e-books, newspapers, magazines, blogs, and other digital media.

clarifying_info.q: What are the specs of the DigiBooks tablet?
clarifying_info.a: DigiBook's tablet uses an e-ink electronic paper display that features 16 shades of grey. This allows for a 12-hour long battery life and easy readability.

clarifying_info.q: Has DigiBooks sold products outside the US before?
clarifying_info.a: No, DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any competitors planning to enter this country?
clarifying_info.a: No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country.

clarifying_info.q: What is the total population and literacy level of the country?
clarifying_info.a: Total population is 76MM with a high literacy level.

exhibits.title: Market Segments
exhibits.shows: A table of three reader segments with segment size (in millions of people) and tablet price point for each segment, plus books read per year per segment.
exhibits.data: Super Readers (SR): 8M people, $200 tablet, 15 books/year; Occasional Readers (OR): 20M people, $125 tablet, 10 books/year; Rare Readers (RR): 10M people, $175 tablet, 5 books/year

exhibits.title: Channel Decisions
exhibits.shows: A table comparing two sales channels (Retail vs. Internet) across four metrics: percent of total potential market, e-book gross margin %, e-reader gross margin %, penetration rate, and initial investment.
exhibits.data: Retail: 50% of total potential market, 50% e-book GM, 30% e-reader GM, 40% penetration, $20M initial investment; Internet: 50% of total potential market, 50% e-book GM, 60% e-reader GM, 10% penetration, $10M initial investment

framework: Segmentation, Targeting & Positioning: Identify which customer segments exist and which is most attractive to target
Product: Assess whether existing product meets local needs or requires adaptation
Price: Determine willingness to pay per segment; consider razor/blade pricing (low tablet price, margin on e-books)
Promotion: Identify marketing mechanisms and channels to build awareness and drive trial
Place/Distribution: Evaluate retail vs. internet sales channels for reach and margin
Content/Selection: Assess availability and breadth of e-book library for this country

questions.prompt: Through research, we found several segments (hand out Exhibit 1). We are only able to target one segment with our product. Using a 3-year projection, which segment should DigiBook target?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 3-year revenue potential per segment (ignoring TVM and probability of purchase unless they surface it as a nuance). Missing data to provide if asked: average e-book price is $10, and e-books and tablets carry the same margin. Revenue = (books/year x $10/book x 3 years + tablet price x 1 tablet) x segment size. Recommend Occasional Readers with $8.5B revenue potential. Bonus: candidate notes TVM or probability of purchase as factors ignored in simplification.

math.setup: Revenue per segment = (books_per_year x $10 x 3 years + tablet_price) x segment_size. E-book price = $10 (to be provided if asked).
steps: SR Revenue = [(15 books x $10 x 3 years) + $200 tablet] x 8M people = [$450 + $200] x 8M = $650 x 8M = $5.2B
OR Revenue = [(10 books x $10 x 3 years) + $125 tablet] x 20M people = [$300 + $125] x 20M = $425 x 20M = $8.5B
RR Revenue = [(5 books x $10 x 3 years) + $175 tablet] x 10M people = [$150 + $175] x 10M = $325 x 10M = $3.25B
math.answer: Target Occasional Readers (OR) with the highest 3-year revenue potential of $8.5B

questions.prompt: DigiBooks is now considering how it should sell its e-book readers: through retail stores or through the internet. How would you go about evaluating this decision?
questions.guidance: Open-ended brainstorm. Candidate should structure pros/cons for each channel. Key retail pros: encourages product trial, joint marketing with retailers, retailer handles customer service/returns. Key retail cons: lower margin due to value chain, time and cost to set up, training costs. Key internet pros: cheaper to establish, higher margins. Key internet cons: harder to encourage trial, requires digital infrastructure/awareness among customers.

questions.prompt: Based on revised market estimates, we decided to price the e-reader at $100 and target the Occasional Reader segment. Using this information and Exhibit 2, can you estimate the 1-year profit potential of each sales channel? Which should we choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute 1-year gross profit minus initial investment for each channel. The OR segment has 20M people; each channel reaches 50% = 10M addressable people. Apply penetration rate to get actual customers. Profit = [(books x e-book price x e-book GM%) + (tablet price x e-reader GM%)] x (addressable market x penetration) - initial investment. Recommend Retail with $300M net profit vs. Internet $100M.

math.setup: Addressable market per channel = 20M OR people x 50% channel share = 10M people. Books/year = 10, e-book price = $10, tablet price = $100.
steps: Retail: Revenue per customer = (10 x $10 x 50% GM) + ($100 x 30% GM) = $50 + $30 = $80. Total profit = $80 x (10M x 40% penetration) = $80 x 4M = $320M. Net = $320M - $20M initial investment = $300M

Internet: Revenue per customer = (10 x $10 x 50% GM) + ($100 x 60% GM) = $50 + $60 = $110. Total profit = $110 x (10M x 10% penetration) = $110 x 1M = $110M. Net = $110M - $10M initial investment = $100M
math.answer: Choose Retail channel with net 1-year profit of $300M vs. Internet $100M

brainstorming.prompt: How would you go about evaluating the retail vs. internet channel decision for DigiBooks?

categories.name: Retail Channel - Pros
ideas: Encourages product trial through physical demonstration
Retailers can assist with joint marketing campaigns
Retailers can handle customer service and returns
Broader reach to customers not comfortable buying online

categories.name: Retail Channel - Cons
ideas: Lower margin due to retailer markup in value chain
Time and money required to establish retail relationships

categories.name: Internet Channel - Pros
ideas: Likely cheaper to establish and maintain
Direct customer relationship and data collection

categories.name: Internet Channel - Cons
ideas: Hard to encourage trial of an unfamiliar product
Requires high internet penetration and digital payment infrastructure
May exclude large portions of population unfamiliar with online shopping
Higher customer acquisition cost through digital marketing

recommendation: DigiBooks should launch in this new country targeting the Occasional Reader segment through the Retail sales channel
This approach yields an estimated 1-year net profit of $300M on a $20M initial investment
risks: Advertising and promotion mechanisms for this new market are not yet defined
Manufacturing and supply chain decisions (local facility vs. export) remain unresolved
Potential future competitor entry could erode first-mover advantage
E-book library selection and local language content availability may limit adoption
next_steps: Define advertising and promotional strategy tailored to this country
Determine sourcing and manufacturing logistics (local vs. export from US)
Assess e-book content library breadth and local language availability
Monitor for potential competitor market entry
